banner.title: bazarr
banner.tagline: Fetches subtitles for the Plex library and saves them beside the media, as UID 2000 on a read-only root filesystem.

explainer.title: A read-only subtitle pipeline over NFS

steps.title: Token
steps.text: ExternalSecret bazarr-secret copies PLEX_TOKEN from the 1Password item plex. An empty token still reports synced, so the decoded length is the real check.
steps.scene: a key being copied from one vault drawer to another

steps.title: Start
steps.text: A busybox init container chowns /run and /tmp. The linuxserver image then runs as UID 2000 with a read-only root filesystem and two emptyDir mounts.
steps.scene: a padlocked server rack with one writable scratch tray

steps.title: Media
steps.text: Bazarr reads the Plex library over NFS at /data/nas-media and the shared downloads at /data/downloads.
steps.scene: a library shelf of film reels linked by a cyan data path

steps.title: Subtitles
steps.text: It searches subtitle providers through its own settings and writes the matching files beside each media file.
steps.scene: a subtitle strip being printed next to a film reel

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: The 5Gi bazarr-config claim, which holds the SQLite database and settings, is backed up by kopiur to Ceph and to R2.
steps.scene: a settings cube sealed into an archive box

art.about: a subtitle service that reads a media library over NFS and writes files beside the media
art.title: How Bazarr fetches subtitles
